March 7, 2023

In Collaboration with GRAMMY Award Nominee Porter Robinson

# Yamaha Releases "Po-uta" Voicebank for VOCALOID™6

Available for Purchase from the Official VOCALOID SHOP from March 7

Yamaha Corporation announces the release of the "Po-uta" voicebank for VOCALOID6, based on vocals from world-renowned singer-songwriter and producer Porter Robinson. Starting from March 7, the new voicebank is available for purchase (download only) from the official VOCALOID SHOP ([https://www.vocaloid.com/en/](https://www.vocaloid.com/en/)). The voicebank is also included in the "Plus Voicebank Set" for VOCALOID6, also available for purchase and download from the official shop.

*   Note: VOCALOID6 has four new VOCALOID:AI-compatible voices exclusive to VOCALOID6 (HARUKA, AKITO, SARAH, ALLEN) and four VOCALOID5 standard voices (Amy, Chris, Kaori, Ken).

## Product Overview

Developed by Yamaha in 2003, VOCALOID singing voice synthesis technology and software creates vocals for songs using lyrics and melodies as input. Synthesizing different vocals is as simple as switching between voicebanks, which are generated from actual human voices. Released in October 2022, VOCALOID6 features the VOCALOID:AI synthesis engine, which uses artificial intelligence to synthesize more natural, richly expressive singing voices. VOCALOID songs created using VOCALOID technology have sparked a new generation of music, boasting countless fans and listeners around the world.

The newly released "Po-uta" voicebank for VOCALOID6 allows users to enjoy creating vocals from artist Porter Robinson, who was nominated for Best Dance Recording in the 61st Annual GRAMMY Awards. The voicebank authentically reproduces the vocals used by Robinson in his own songs, which are known for their clarity and exquisite high range. This ensures a striking presence that won't be eclipsed, even by powerful music such as electronica. Using VOCALOID's "Style Presets" feature, users can also choose from thirteen singing style presets, approved by Robinson himself, to automatically adjust the vocal style, tone, and more. This makes it possible to recreate the vocals used in hits like "Shelter" or "Musician" with ease. The voicebank also supports new VOCALOID6 features, such as VOCALO CHANGER, which uses the creator's vocal data to replicate their own singing style as-is, and Multilingual, which makes it possible to sing lyrics in a mixture of fluent Japanese, English, and Chinese with a single voicebank.

**Vocaloid 6**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_6#cite_note-2) is a [singing vocal synthesizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singing "Singing") application developed by [Yamaha Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamaha_Corporation "Yamaha Corporation"). The successor to [Vocaloid 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_5 "Vocaloid 5") in the [Vocaloid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid "Vocaloid") series, it is the first to incorporate [machine learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning "Machine learning"), branded as Vocaloid:AI.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vocaloid_6&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

After scheduled maintenance of the official Vocaloid website on October 13, 2022, Yamaha released Vocaloid 6 without prior announcement.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_6#cite_note-3)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_6#cite_note-4) It introduces the Vocaloid:AI engine, which had been in development since around [Vocaloid 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_3 "Vocaloid 3") and was first publicly shown in a concert, reviving the voice of deceased singer [Hibari Misora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hibari_Misora "Hibari Misora").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_6#cite_note-5) Voices developed for it offer improved synthesis quality, multilingual singing and drastically smaller file sizes. Support for older voices from Vocaloid 3 and up remains. It also features the addition of Vocalo Changer, a tool that converts the voice from a singing recording into that of a Vocaloid voice. Other additions are support for ARA 2 and an updated UI. A trial was released on the same day.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_6#cite_note-6)

### Adachi Rei

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vocaloid_6&action=edit&section=33 "Edit section: Adachi Rei")]

After successfully building a life-size [Hatsune Miku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hatsune_Miku "Hatsune Miku") robot, Japanese creator Missile began work on an original character robot, named [Adachi Rei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adachi_Rei "Adachi Rei")[[ja](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E8%B6%B3%E7%AB%8B%E3%83%AC%E3%82%A4 "ja:足立レイ")], for which he synthesized a feminine Utau voicebank from scratch in Audacity. Officially released for Japanese, voicebanks for other languages, including English, Spanish, and French, have been created by the community. After a successful crowdfund, a pair of Vocaloid voicebanks, a Vocaloid 5 voicebank utilizing [concatenative synthesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concatenative_synthesis "Concatenative synthesis") and a Vocaloid 6 voicebank incorporating [machine learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning "Machine learning"), were announced. They are among several Vocaloid voicebanks announced but not yet released, but among those are the only ones released in early access, and are planned for a 2026 release.

**Vocaloid 6**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_6#cite_note-2) is a [singing vocal synthesizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singing "Singing") application developed by [Yamaha Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamaha_Corporation "Yamaha Corporation"). The successor to [Vocaloid 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_5 "Vocaloid 5") in the [Vocaloid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid "Vocaloid") series, it is the first to incorporate [machine learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning "Machine learning"), branded as Vocaloid:AI.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vocaloid_6&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

After scheduled maintenance of the official Vocaloid website on October 13, 2022, Yamaha released Vocaloid 6 without prior announcement.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_6#cite_note-3)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_6#cite_note-4) It introduces the Vocaloid:AI engine, which had been in development since around [Vocaloid 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_3 "Vocaloid 3") and was first publicly shown in a concert, reviving the voice of deceased singer [Hibari Misora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hibari_Misora "Hibari Misora").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_6#cite_note-5) Voices developed for it offer improved synthesis quality, multilingual singing and drastically smaller file sizes. Support for older voices from Vocaloid 3 and up remains. It also features the addition of Vocalo Changer, a tool that converts the voice from a singing recording into that of a Vocaloid voice. Other additions are support for ARA 2 and an updated UI. A trial was released on the same day.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_6#cite_note-6)

## Products

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vocaloid_6&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Products")]

### Haruka, Akito, Sarah, and Allen

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vocaloid_6&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Haruka, Akito, Sarah, and Allen")]

A pair of English voicebanks and a pair of Japanese voicebanks, one each masculine and feminine. They come bundled with the Vocaloid 6 software and act as the program's default voices.

### AI Megpoid

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vocaloid_6&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: AI Megpoid")]

An update for [Megpoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megpoid "Megpoid"), a Japanese feminine voicebank developed by [Internet Co., Ltd.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_Co.,_Ltd. "Internet Co., Ltd.") based on the voice of [Megumi Nakajima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megumi_Nakajima "Megumi Nakajima"). It was released on October 13, 2022.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_6#cite_note-7) Megpoid voicebanks have previously been released for [Vocaloid 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_2 "Vocaloid 2"), [Vocaloid 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_3 "Vocaloid 3"), [Vocaloid 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_4 "Vocaloid 4"), and [Synthesizer V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthesizer_V "Synthesizer V"). An append named AI Megpoid Solid was released separately on July 4, 2024.

### Po-uta

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vocaloid_6&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Po-uta")]

A masculine English-focused voicebank based on the voice of singer [Porter Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porter_Robinson "Porter Robinson"), developed as a collaboration between Sample Sized, LLC and Yamaha Corporation. It was released on March 7, 2023.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_6#cite_note-8)

### Fuiro

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vocaloid_6&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Fuiro")]

A Japanese feminine voicebank based on singer philo, also known as Taki Takota, made as a collaboration between Yamaha Corporation and nana Music Co., Ltd., that released on May 9, 2023.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_6#cite_note-9)

### ZOLA Project

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vocaloid_6&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: ZOLA Project")]

[ZOLA Project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZOLA_Project "ZOLA Project") is a bundle of three Japanese masculine voicebanks, Yuu, Kyo and Wil, developed by Yamaha Corporation. Originally released for Vocaloid 3 in 2013, for Vocaloid's 10th anniversary, their Vocaloid 6 versions were released on June 20, 2023, the exact 10th anniversary of their Vocaloid 3 release.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_6#cite_note-10)

### AI Otomachi Una

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vocaloid_6&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: AI Otomachi Una")]

An update for [Otomachi Una](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otomachi_Una "Otomachi Una"), a feminine Japanese voicebank based on the voice of Aimi Tanaka and developed by Internet Co., Ltd., that released on June 22, 2023.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_6#cite_note-11) Previously released voicebanks for Vocaloid 4, Voiceroid 2]], and Synthesizer V, among others.

### Sakura, Asahi, Shion, and Taku

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vocaloid_6&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Sakura, Asahi, Shion, and Taku")]

A collection of further Japanese default voicebanks, two masculine and two feminine, that have been included with Vocaloid 6 since update 6.3.0, released on December 24, 2023.

### Michelle and Lucas

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vocaloid_6&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Michelle and Lucas")]

Two English default voicebanks, one masculine and one feminine, added in update 6.3.1a, released on February 19, 2024.

### AI Hibiki Koto

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vocaloid_6&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: AI Hibiki Koto")]

Hibiki Koto is a Japanese feminine voicebank developed by Internet Co., Ltd. and released on April 18, 2024. Followed the same year by a [Synthesizer V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthesizer_V "Synthesizer V") voicebank.

### Shiki Rowen AI

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vocaloid_6&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Shiki Rowen AI")]

A Japanese masculine voicebank developed by Mugen Co., Ltd. and released on April 24, 2024.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_6#cite_note-12) Previously had several voicebanks for [Utau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utau "Utau") and other software, many under the name Kemonone Row.

### GekiyakuV and KazehikiV

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vocaloid_6&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: GekiyakuV and KazehikiV")]

Two Japanese voicebanks, masculine and feminine, developed by Kuzutokaze and Yamaha Corporation, released on July 18, 2024.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocaloid_6#cite_note-13) Both originally released for [Utau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utau "Utau"), and were included in the experimental Vocaloid plugin VX-β.

### Galaco Black and Galaco White

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vocaloid_6&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Galaco Black and Galaco White")]

### Adachi Rei

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vocaloid_6&action=edit&section=33 "Edit section: Adachi Rei")]

After successfully building a life-size [Hatsune Miku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hatsune_Miku "Hatsune Miku") robot, Japanese creator Missile began work on an original character robot, named [Adachi Rei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adachi_Rei "Adachi Rei")[[ja](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E8%B6%B3%E7%AB%8B%E3%83%AC%E3%82%A4 "ja:足立レイ")], for which he synthesized a feminine Utau voicebank from scratch in Audacity. Officially released for Japanese, voicebanks for other languages, including English, Spanish, and French, have been created by the community. After a successful crowdfund, a pair of Vocaloid voicebanks, a Vocaloid 5 voicebank utilizing [concatenative synthesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concatenative_synthesis "Concatenative synthesis") and a Vocaloid 6 voicebank incorporating [machine learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning "Machine learning"), were announced. They are among several Vocaloid voicebanks announced but not yet released, but among those are the only ones released in early access, and are planned for a 2026 release.
